Consider the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,$ shown above. Given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

find the value of $a-b.$
worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use the formula for differentiating parametric curves:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}
$$

First, we recall that to convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Using the fact that $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ y & =(3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

where we used the identity $\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$ 

To compute our derivative, we first need to calculate ${x}^{′}(\theta )$ and ${y}^{′}(\theta ):$ 

- First, we compute the derivative of $x$ with respect to $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\theta ) & ={(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta )}^{′}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{′} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta \cdot 2)+2(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute the derivative of $y$ with respect to $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta ) & ={(3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & ={(3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}^{′}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{′} \\  & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )+(-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a=2,b=-2,$ and so 

$$
a-b=2-(-2)=4.
$$
